title: The runtime condition-repair turn (run-5 solution 2)
goal: Implement solution 2 from the run-5 analysis: when the verification battery reports the active subtask's OUTCOME achieved while its code done-condition is unmet, run ONE bounded condition-repair turn (a repair-only planner call + a code fallback), validate/check the repaired condition on the current observation, require the battery's concurrence, and accept/advance (or extract the report) instead of only re-planning. No device/emulator test until the owner explicitly says.

WI1-trigger-and-bounded-repair-framework.detail: VisionLoop: the hook is EXACTLY the battery block's BatteryGate.OutcomeAchieved branch; RedFlags and Proceed are untouched. The one-per-(active subtask, plan) allowance lives in the class-field `repairAttempted` set keyed by the subtask pointer, cleared on the accept advance (inside the shared `acceptAdvance`), on every new plan install (the re-plan block) and at run start. A failed/invalid turn falls through to the existing battery re-plan path unchanged (battery budget + held-step guard intact). Acceptance: the repaired condition is checked with DoneConditionChecker.satisfied on the CURRENT observation AND batteryConcurs over THIS step's results. It is an ACCEPT path (no executor call, no gate); the advance/terminal semantics moved into the shared local `acceptAdvance` used BY THE NORMAL ACCEPT TOO (same pointer/consecutiveFailures/recentHashes/stepsOnSubtask/subtaskStartHash/actionHistory/verbHistory/batteryReplans/lastBatteryResults/lastBatteryHash/step resets; the final subtask extracts when the ladder carries answerExtracted, then GOAL_ACHIEVED). The weak-at-start gate is deliberately bypassed ONLY for the repaired-condition acceptance (documented loudly in code): the battery saw the outcome after the subtask's own actions and is the arrival evidence. Step line emitted exactly `step N: CONDITION REPAIRED - '<old render>' -> '<new render>' (the outcome was visible)` into outcomes + events.log + the corner log, plus `subtask N/M DONE (condition repaired)`.

WI2-repair-source.detail: VisionPrompts: `REPAIR_SYSTEM` (repair-only; the OUTCOME law, the six whitelisted shapes, the no-clock/no-date law, the never-a-mention law, the untrusted-page law) + `repairUser(instruction, doneText, pageDigest, outcomeEvidence)` + `parseRepairedCondition` reusing LadderSchema.parseDoneConditionText; `VISION_PROMPT_VERSION` v11 -> v12. VisionLoop.conditionRepairTurn: ONE VisionHaiku.chat with the current screenshot, `call repair` raw req/res evidence; the user message carries the page digest, the active subtask, the old done condition and the code-assembled <jev-evidence> block (escalation pinned to OUTCOME-ACHIEVED-WHILE-CONDITION-UNMET). Invalid shape or a valid-but-non-matching condition -> NoAccept -> the existing re-plan path. Code fallback ONLY when the planner CALL fails: the current readable URL host under the checker's normalization, else the longest visible page line as markerText; checked on the current evidence and recorded `condition repair: code-derived fallback -> <render>`. No date is ever derived or accepted by prompt law; date-shaped conditions that do not match fail the check.

WI3-tests.detail: NEW VisionLoopConditionRepairTest (8 tests, $0 scripted, fabricated capture, temp-dir evidence): (1) OutcomeAchieved + vague elementPresent + visible-marker repair accepts, advances, exact step line, call-003-repair raw bodies, run reaches the terminal; (2a) invalid repair shape -> no accept, existing battery re-plan path, no fallback; (2b) valid-but-non-matching repair -> no accept, existing re-plan path; (3) failed repair call (maxRetries=0) -> code-derived URL-host fallback accepts; (4) a second OutcomeAchieved on the same subtask/plan never calls the repair again (call repair count 1, the allowance line); (5) the repaired results subtask advances to the final answerExtracted, extracts exactly once, ends GOAL_ACHIEVED with the answer; (6) a red-flag escalation never calls the repair; (7) a marker present only on an earlier page does not accept (current-observation-only check). deviations: WI2 says the code fallback runs 'only when the planner call fails or is invalid', while the Parse+validate bullet and WI3-2 pin 'invalid shape or non-matching condition -> NO acceptance -> the existing re-plan path'. Implemented: the fallback runs ONLY on a planner CALL failure (transport/HTTP/malformed response). A parse-invalid shape or a valid-but-non-matching condition takes the existing re-plan path with NO fallback (test 2a deliberately offers a readable URL host, so an unlawful fallback would have accepted). This follows the phase's own acceptance tests and the explicit Parse+validate bullet.

The one-repair allowance resets on a NEW PLAN INSTALL, so a re-plan-resumed subtask becomes eligible again by law. WI3-4's second-OutcomeAchieved case therefore scripts the same plan: the battery budget is 0, so the fall-through takes the existing battery path's forced-PROCEED arm instead of installing a plan (a successful battery re-plan would reset the allowance). The test still pins the load-bearing fact: exactly ONE `call repair` on the same (subtask, plan), and the second trigger names the spent allowance.

The repaired accept does NOT call recordedOpinions (no extra Jev noul / Haiku confirm): the acceptance evidence is the repaired code check + the trigger battery's concurrence. The normal accept-line semantics ride as `subtask N/M DONE (condition repaired)` without a model opinion (the old-condition opinion would usually disagree with the repair by construction).

The code fallback's URL host reuses the public DoneConditionChecker.normalizeUrl (the checker's own normalization) and requires a dotted host, matching DoneConditionChecker.hostOf's rules, rather than widening :core's internal hostOf to public.
The code-derived markerText is capped at LadderLimits.MAX_CONDITION_TEXT_CHARS (300) for whitelist coherence; the derivation prefers the longest non-blank visible line.

A failed repair leaves the existing BATTERY ESCALATE line and the re-plan <jev-evidence> block unchanged (the phase's 'probe/evidence unchanged'); it adds one loud `condition repair: ... - the existing battery path runs` evidence event for monitoring.

The parser reuses LadderSchema's existing behavior for a multi-key blend (the first matching whitelist shape wins) instead of adding a new strictness rule; the test pins that behavior rather than inventing a rejection.
No device/emulator/adb/install/live calls; no commit (owner hold).
